title: opportunity-matrix-and-quote-synthesis-sep-2025
summary: Concise synthesis of customer feedback from Aug–Sep 2025 focused on Private deployments, latency/cost tradeoffs, and rollout controls. Maps direct customer quotes to candidate features and commercial hypotheses, with recommended next-step probes and owners.
background: We ran a focused VOC sweep targeting 12 mid/enterprise customers that recently trialed Redwood Private or migrated a portion of traffic to Redwood Dedicated. Interviews + support threads surfaced recurring themes: friction onboarding private networks, KV cache/memory tuning uncertainty, and unpredictable cost spikes during bursts. This doc converts qualitative threads into an opportunity matrix and prioritized request list tied to impact/effort hypotheses.
methodology: Sources: 12 account interviews (recorded), 34 support tickets (Jul–Sep 2025), two SRE postmortems for latency incidents. We annotated quotes, clustered asks, and scored each candidate feature by (customer frequency, estimated $impact, engineering effort). Scoring heuristics are intentionally coarse to guide next-step experiments.
opportunity_matrix_highlights:
1) Private onboarding checklist + network sanity tool (high frequency, medium effort, high impact) 
2) Burst-cost visibility + predictive alerting (medium frequency, low effort, high impact) 
3) KV cache prescriptive profiles + one-click warmers (low-medium frequency, medium effort, medium impact) 
4) Rollout canary templates with traffic shaping by model variant (low frequency, high effort, high impact for enterprise customers)
prioritized_requests: Private onboarding diagnoser: automated network checks, common NAT/VPC issue hints, and a single-run connectivity report for SREs (Customer demand: high among large regulated customers; Impact: reduces onboarding time by estimated 30%; Effort: medium).

Burst cost forecasting and alerting: schedule-based/traffic-pattern detectors to surface impending cost deltas before spikes (Customer demand: medium; Impact: prevents surprise bills, improves renewal conversations; Effort: low).

KV cache profiles: prebuilt cache/quantization profiles matched to workload archetypes (chat, long-form assistant, streaming generation) and a toggle to apply them (Customer demand: medium; Impact: token-cost reduction, latency stability; Effort: medium).

Canary rollouts with shard-level traffic shaping: templates for safe rollouts across private/dedicated pools, including automatic fallback to hosted model variants (Customer demand: strategic enterprise accounts; Impact: reduces rollback risk; Effort: high).

Request-level cost attribution in Console: per-route token-cost breakdown tied to model variant and quantization profile (Customer demand: high for platform teams; Impact: better cost governance; Effort: low-medium).
customer_quotes: "We spent a week chasing NAT rules — if Redwood had a one-click network sniff, we would have onboarded in a day." — Platform lead, regulated fintech
"Our costs shot up during a weekend batch run. We didn't even get an early signal. The bill came as a surprise." — ML infra manager, mid-market marketplace
"KV cache tuning feels like witchcraft — we need prescriptive profiles, not guess-and-check." — Senior ML engineer, conversational AI startup
"Canarying a model felt manual — we had to build traffic split logic ourselves to avoid affecting latency for live users." — Engineering manager, enterprise search provider
action_items: Draft PRD for Private onboarding diagnoser: owner Maya Patel, due 2025-09-26.
Spike: cost-forecasting prototype using last-90-day traffic windows — owner Evan Cho, prototype demo 2025-09-19.
Run pilot with two enterprise customers for KV cache profiles (Priya Narayanan to run outreach, Diego Alvarez to own config templates) — outreach by 2025-09-15.
Create Console mockups for per-route cost attribution and present at product review 2025-09-22 (owner: product-hosted-api design lead).
risk_and_open_questions: 1) Telemetry completeness for accurate cost forecasting — do we have token-level traces for private deployments? 2) Security review for any network diagnoser that runs remote checks — legal and security signoff required. 3) Backwards compatibility for older agent integrations using custom KV cache code.
commercial_hypotheses: If we deliver onboarding diagnoser and burst-cost alerts, we expect a 10–15% reduction in ramp time for Private deals and a 5–8% improvement in renewal NRR for tiered enterprise accounts. These features also create a new up-sell lane for enhanced onboarding support.
recommended_next_steps: Validate telemetry availability with infra team (ticket JIRA-INF-1187).
Build a 2-week spike for cost-forecasting and demo results to two customers (Evan Cho).
Schedule security review for the diagnoser concept; prepare threat model (security-and-compliance).
Prepare a one-page customer-facing framing (value props + sample quote) to use in sales conversations; hand to GTM by 2025-09-20.
notes_for_engineering: Prefer minimal-surface spikes first: console surface for cost alerts + a CLI-based network diagnoser that runs locally in the customer's VPC. Keep prototype telemetry ingestion isolated from customer data — use aggregated counters for early tests.
final_words: This is a working synthesis intended to convert scattered customer voice into actionable probes. Please add missing quotes, flag incorrect attributions, and push edits to the linked Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-4321).
